newsitem.title: INDIA: India to hear Rao case on alleged vote-buying.
newsitem.headline: India to hear Rao case on alleged vote-buying.

text.p: India's federal police said on Friday that a case believed to involve former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and his Congress party in an alleged vote buying scandal would be heard by a local court next week.
"We are going to submit our report to the Delhi High Court. The matter will be coming up before the court on Monday," said S.M. Khan, spokesman for the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI).
Lawmakers of the regional Jharkand Mukti Morcha (JMM) party had said they been paid $100,000 to vote against a 1993 no-confidence motion that Rao's Congress-led government narrowly survived.
In June, the CBI filed a police case containing charges that Rao and other Congress leaders bought the votes.
Rao resigned as prime minister in May after the Congress party lost the general elections.
"We are not commenting whether we have questioned Rao or not" in connection with the case, Khan said.
The United News of India said one JMM member of parliament and two former party members were arrested on Thursday in connection with the case. There was no official confirmation.
Newspaper reports, however, said the CBI had questioned Rao on the alleged vote-buying case in recent days.
"According to sources, Rao was questioned by CBI officials on 23 points. He is reported to have denied any role in the pay-offs," the Asian Age newspaper said.
Congress party officials could not be reached for comment.
The Asian Age also said the CBI had already questioned a state chief minister, three former union ministers, and one industrialist on the scandal.
"I have the right to remain silent," the Pioneer newspaper quoted Rao as saying while he was questioned by the CBI.
It said he was questioned for 45 minutes.
The CBI did not mention Rao in an earlier report based on a complaint in February by an anti-corruption citizens' group. Four former ministers in Rao's cabinet were named in the case.
In May, the Delhi High Court ordered the CBI to file a fresh report based on the complaint and to speed up the investigation.
